outlook.statement: During the current financial year, your Company is making all possible efforts to improve the performance.
During current year, your Company will try to improve the performance with applying optimistic efforts.
The Indian alcohol market has been flourishing since the early 2000s... ensuring strong growth for spirits producers well into the next decade.
The Indian liquor industry is poised for growth and expected grow @ 5% to 6% per Annum, driven by a combination of demographic shifts, urbanization trends, and rising income levels.

risks: Recoverability of Rs. 2,900.25 Lakhs classified as 'Other Non-Current Assets' under dispute; SEBI directed parties to repay; auditor unable to comment on reliability/recoverability and no provision for Expected Credit Loss
Government regulations affect the Indian Liquor industry introducing structural rigidities
High level taxes and levies
Regulations pertaining to licensing creation or expanding of brewing/distillery and bottling capacities, manufacturing process (grain based and molasses based), distribution and advertising

Liquor being a state subject, every state has different regulations (including those on distribution) and tax rate for the industry apart from restrictions as well as levies on the inter-state movement of liquor

The India-European Union Free Trade Agreement signed in January 2026 significantly slashes steep import duties on European wines, spirits, and beers, making foreign alcohol cheaper and more accessible for Indian consumer
Government is introducing some new licenses for new business entrants which poses a competition risk for the Company's product
Intense competition prevails in the segment, fuelled by the lucrative growth prospects of the industry
Regulatory hurdles, high taxation, and restrictions on advertising alcoholic beverages
Multiple regulatory considerations with respect to pricing, licensing, plant set-up, marketing & advertising and distribution creating barriers to entry
Delay in appointment of Company Secretary beyond the prescribed period of 3 months from the date of vacancy, resulting in non-compliance with Regulation 6 of SEBI (LODR), 2015.
